A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Alexandria. Their complete text, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, automatic translation benchmarks, human evaluations, and translator-survey results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds NLLB comparisons, metadata ablations, linguistic diagnostics, and translation-revision examples.

M1.justification: The Gemini-2.5-Pro source-generation pipeline, human translation, peer revision, and normalization remain unchanged. The metadata ablations test evaluation conditions rather than introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Both cover English-dialectal Arabic translation across the same 13 countries, city-level varieties, and 11 domains. The added experiments analyze existing dialect subsets and data characteristics rather than introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds NLLB-200-3.3B against Gemma-3-12B-IT, Aya-Expanse-32B, and Command-A across nine existing dialects. v1 explicitly excluded traditional MT baselines. The original 24-LLM comparison pool is retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds single-turn None, gender-only, and Full metadata conditions, plus diagnostics using NLLB-generated MSA and Latin-character stratification. Existing splits, metrics, decoding, and human-rating procedures remain. Reported corpus counts change, including 6,050 generated turns becoming 6,050 conversations per country; these revisions do not establish that existing benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: Metadata ablations in Table 3, MSA-overlap and code-switching analyses in Tables 4-5, and paired revision examples in Table A.1 substantially expand the diagnostic evidence. The reasoning, input-context, domain, and sub-dialect analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Agreement measures, overlapping annotation samples, and statistical reporting practices remain unchanged. Revision AC1 is 0.65 in both versions; the apparent trailing 5/6 are footnote markers. New correlation results do not introduce a specified new estimation procedure, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 3-5 add substantial baseline, metadata, and linguistic-diagnostic results. For example, Table 3 reports Egyptian spBLEU of 17.16 for NLLB versus 25.54 for Gemma-3-12B without metadata. The conversation count changes from 33,500 to 34,488, and Table 2 revises country/domain counts. Existing automatic benchmark and human-evaluation result values are retained.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, mathematical definitions, theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations are added or revised. The additions concern empirical comparisons and diagnostics.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a community-created, approximately 107K-turn benchmark with geographic, domain, and gender annotations that exposes persistent dialectal translation challenges. Updated corpus counts and additional supporting experiments do not redefine that contribution.

C2.justification: New discussion describes metadata benefits as model- and dialect-dependent and relates performance to MSA lexical overlap and code-switching. The limitation excluding traditional MT baselines is removed following the NLLB comparison. Existing interpretations of directional asymmetry and semantic adequacy versus dialectal authenticity remain.

D1.justification: v1's introduction offers dataset samples, prompts, guidelines, and evaluation code; v2's abstract states that the dataset itself is publicly available at the same repository. This expands the reported availability beyond relocating the link. Most implementation and annotation details are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds Malaysha et al. (2024), AraFinNLP. Broader research positioning remains largely unchanged. Consolidating duplicate Fanar references and expanding NLLB bibliographic metadata do not change cited-work membership.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial structural reorganization: source-quality assurance becomes Section 3.1.2, project management becomes Section 3.4, and reasoning discussion moves into Section 5.1. Appendix headings are restructured, alongside copyediting and abstract, author, and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and four existing appendix plots move into the main text: t-SNE, code-mixing, input-setting comparisons, and reasoning effects. v2 adds Tables 3-5 and revision-example Table A.1, with extensive relocation, renumbering, and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The NLLB comparison and metadata controls address part of v1's acknowledged baseline limitation, while paired revision examples improve transparency. These provide a clear, focused quality gain. Some new interpretations remain overbroad: Aya with Full metadata falls below NLLB for Moroccan and Tunisian Arabic despite blanket outperformance wording, and the linguistic correlations support associations rather than causal explanations.
